title: Cost engineering: useful-task budgets and routing
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects cost engineering: useful-task budgets and routing with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Produce a cost-quality-latency comparison for baseline, cached, routed and shortened-context variants.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: AI cost includes input/output tokens, embedding/indexing work, retries, agent steps, evaluation and human review. Price per token is only one input to cost per accepted task. Smaller models, shorter context and caching help only if they preserve the required outcome.
A routing policy sends simple cases to a low-cost path and escalates difficult or uncertain cases. Routing must be evaluated for false confidence, not merely average savings.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Set per-task and monthly budgets using dated provider rates. Track measured usage rather than estimating solely from characters. Cache authorized deterministic work and stable retrieval results, batch offline embedding jobs and reduce duplicate context.

Use confidence thresholds calibrated on held-out cases to route accepted classifications, uncertain cases to stronger analysis and unsupported cases to humans. Bound agent steps and judge calls as part of the same budget.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A cheap classifier confidently mislabels product defects as automation issues, lowering billed cost while increasing operational risk. An optimization removes the evidence needed for correct answers. A cache saves tokens but serves stale permissions.
Compare accepted accuracy, abstention, review labor and total spend before and after optimization. Include cold-start/indexing costs and failed attempts in the report.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Produce a cost-quality-latency comparison for baseline, cached, routed and shortened-context variants. Reject candidates that violate hard safety or quality constraints even if they are cheaper.
SDETs should validate budget enforcement with synthetic high-usage responses and ensure over-budget tasks terminate or degrade visibly rather than continuing hidden work.

mistake: A cheap classifier confidently mislabels product defects as automation issues, lowering billed cost while increasing operational risk. An optimization removes the evidence needed for correct answers. A cache saves tokens but serves stale permissions.
takeaway: Produce a cost-quality-latency comparison for baseline, cached, routed and shortened-context variants.

title: Enforce task budgets before hidden work grows
objectives: Enforce task budgets before hidden work grows
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects enforce task budgets before hidden work grows with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance includes bounded work, dated rate configuration and measured usage artifacts.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A task budget bounds total attempts and their resource use, not only the final accepted response. Retries, discarded generations, judge calls and agent tools all contribute. A request can stay within each component's local limit while exceeding the user's total allowance.

Estimates and measured usage serve different purposes. Reserve estimated capacity before work, then reconcile actual usage returned by the provider. Rates are dated configuration; this course does not embed current pricing as a permanent fact.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Track remaining input/output token allowance, call count, wall time and estimated currency cost in task state. Refuse or degrade before beginning work that cannot fit the budget. Include cached-token and reasoning usage according to provider accounting rather than guessing.

Calculate cost per accepted task over all attempts. Compare routing and caching variants on the same dataset with quality and privacy constraints held fixed. A low billed cost that increases wrong automated decisions is not a successful optimization.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: An agent gives each retry a fresh token limit and never reconciles total usage. A judge runs on every intermediate draft, multiplying spend. A cache uses tenant-free keys and saves cost by leaking evidence.

Test budget exhaustion before and after a provider response, duplicated retries and negative/invalid usage values. Ensure the visible status explains budget termination rather than claiming a completed investigation.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance includes bounded work, dated rate configuration and measured usage artifacts. Report total spend, accepted tasks, abstentions and review load together.
For SDETs, budgets are deterministic state invariants that can be tested with synthetic usage events. Live provider measurements then establish actual operating cost under the declared workload.

mistake: An agent gives each retry a fresh token limit and never reconciles total usage. A judge runs on every intermediate draft, multiplying spend. A cache uses tenant-free keys and saves cost by leaking evidence.
takeaway: Acceptance includes bounded work, dated rate configuration and measured usage artifacts.
